items.title: Home Screen app keeps the screen on
items.summary: Drive for five minutes without touching the iPad; the screen must stay on.
items.why: The Home Screen app and its wake lock have only been tried on a desk. A screen that sleeps mid-lap loses the coach card.
prerequisites: Open Pitwall on the iPad from its Home Screen icon (added from the Tailscale address in Safari: Share › Add to Home Screen).

steps.text: On the iPad, set Settings › Display & Brightness › Auto-Lock to 2 minutes for this test.
Open Drive › Coach.
Drive for at least 5 minutes without touching the iPad.
Watch that the screen stays on and no "Screen may sleep" chip appears.
Afterwards put Auto-Lock back to what you had.

attestations.text: I did not touch the iPad while driving

items.prompt: Did the screen stay on the whole time?
items.radio_brief: Validation: screen test. Drive five minutes without touching the iPad.

informs.status_md: Dashboard v2 › Unverified: Home Screen app, wake lock

items.rule_text: While this test is current the iPad reports every 15 seconds. This passes when the page stayed visible on a Drive page with the wake lock on and telemetry live from the console for at least 5 minutes (heuristic), opened from the Home Screen icon over HTTPS, with no report more than 45 seconds late. It fails when the page was hidden or went quiet while you were driving and you say you did not touch the iPad.

items.title: Glance test at 70 cm (each driver)
items.summary: Each driver reads the next corner, the delta and the coaching point from quick glances.
items.why: Glanceability at 70 cm is the main promise of the new dashboard and has not been tried on the rig.
prerequisites: iPad on its mount at about 70 cm, the lights as when you race.

steps.text: Drive 3 laps on Drive › Coach.
From quick glances, say the next corner and whether a braking call is coming.
Say whether the time gap (delta) shows plus or minus, and its first number.
Read the coaching point on a straight.
Answer: what did you look at first?

attestations.text: I could read the next corner and whether a call was coming
I could read whether the delta was plus or minus, and its first number
I could read the coaching point on a straight

items.prompt: Could you read everything you needed at a glance?
items.radio_brief: Validation: glance test. Three laps on Drive, Coach. Glance at the iPad as you would in a race.

informs.status_md: Dashboard v2 › glance and family tests (spec 14.5)

items.rule_text: Only you can judge what you read at a glance. Pitwall shows the laps each driver drove during this test (3 or more (heuristic)) and whether the iPad was on Drive › Coach.

items.title: Screen and radio give the same coaching point
items.summary: Five laps with the radio live: the coach card and the engineer must give the same point.
items.why: The coach card and the engineer should pick the same coaching point; that has not been seen live.
prerequisites: Radio live (Drive › Radio › Go live), coaching Normal.

steps.text: Drive 5 laps.
When the engineer gives a coaching point, check the coach card shows the same corner and advice.

items.prompt: Did the card and the radio always agree?
items.radio_brief: Validation: one message test. Five laps; check the coach card matches what I say.

informs.status_md: Dashboard v2 › D6 not yet seen live

items.rule_text: For each lap Pitwall knows which points the coach card picked. Every coaching point the radio started to play must be one of them. This passes after 3 such points with none different; one different point fails.

items.title: One hour on Drive
items.summary: Keep Drive open for an hour of driving with the radio live.
items.why: Long sessions on the iPad (heat, memory, reloads) have not been tried.

steps.text: Keep Drive › Coach open for an hour of driving with the radio live.

items.prompt: Did the screen stay smooth for the whole hour?
items.radio_brief: Validation: endurance test. Keep Drive open for an hour of driving.

informs.status_md: Dashboard v2 › spec 14.5 #7 (one hour on Drive)

items.rule_text: While this test is current and a Drive page is open, the iPad reports its frame rate every 10 seconds. This passes after an hour (360 reports) with 90 % of them at 45 fps or more (heuristic) and no reload. Memory use is not available in Safari.

items.title: Push-to-talk over Tailscale with an AirPod
items.summary: Ask the engineer three questions, from the screen and from your wheel button.
items.why: Speech input on the iPad is still a pending driver test, and the React radio has not been used over Tailscale HTTPS.
prerequisites: One AirPod paired with the iPad and in your ear.
Pitwall opened from the Tailscale address (the Home Screen icon is fine).

steps.text: Drive › Radio › Go live; allow the microphone.
Hold the on-screen talk button, ask "How are my tyres?", let go.
Hold your wheel's talk button and ask "Where am I losing the most time?"
Ask one more question while driving.
When you stop, mark each transcript below as heard right or wrong.

attestations.text: The AirPod was the microphone and the speaker

items.prompt: Did the engineer hear you and answer sensibly?
items.radio_brief: Validation: push-to-talk. Ask me two questions, one with your wheel button.

informs.status_md: Phase 5 › Speech input (PTT) on the iPad: pending driver test
Dashboard v2 › push-to-talk over Tailscale HTTPS

items.rule_text: A round trip is a question heard, answered and starting to play on the iPad. This passes after 2 round trips (heuristic) on the iPad opened over Tailscale HTTPS, with an AirPod as the microphone (from its name, or your tick) and at most 1 in 3 questions not heard (heuristic). Three attempts with no round trip fail. Quick answers should start within 4 s and engineer answers within 20 s (heuristic): shown as warnings.
items.unavailable_reason: Voice is off on this Mac.

items.title: The radio keeps out of braking zones
items.summary: Five laps with the radio live: lap summaries and coaching must start and end on straights.
items.why: Proactive timing has only been tested on generated data.
prerequisites: Radio live, coaching Normal or Detailed.

steps.text: Drive 5 or more clean laps and listen.
Lap summaries and coaching should start and finish on straights, never into a braking zone or a corner.

items.prompt: Did the radio keep out of braking zones and corners?
items.radio_brief: Validation: speak windows. Five laps; notice if I talk into a braking zone.

informs.status_md: Phase 5 › proactive message timing: synthetic only

items.rule_text: For each lap summary or coaching point Pitwall reads your brake and steering while it played, from the stored lap. Brake at 0.10 or more or steering beyond 0.25 (heuristic) is an overlap; ending less than 0.5 s (heuristic) before the next braking is tight. This passes with 6 messages measured on track over 3 laps (heuristic), no overlap and at most 1 tight. Two overlaps, or one into braking of 0.5 or more (heuristic), fail.
items.unavailable_reason: Voice is off on this Mac.

items.title: Natural engineer voice heard on track
items.summary: Three laps listening to the natural voice: lap times, coaching and braking calls.
items.why: The neural voice has not been heard in a live session.
prerequisites: Settings › Radio & voice › Engineer voice: this Mac; Mac voice: bm_fable (or another natural voice).

steps.text: Drive 3 or more laps with the radio live.
Listen to lap times, coaching and braking calls.
Note any word or number that sounded wrong.

attestations.text: Numbers and corner names were clear

items.prompt: Did the natural voice sound right on track?
items.radio_brief: Validation: natural voice. Three laps; listen for any word or number that sounds wrong.

informs.status_md: Neural radio voice › not heard live yet

items.rule_text: Pitwall counts messages the natural voice rendered that reached the iPad as audio and started playing. This passes with 5 such messages (heuristic), at most 20 % (heuristic) in the fallback voice, no restart of the voice worker, and the iPad set to the Mac's voice.
items.unavailable_reason: Voice is off on this Mac.

items.title: Braking calls land on time
items.summary: Three laps with calls off, then three to five with calls on: the call must land at or just before your braking point.
items.why: Live braking calls are tested on generated and recorded data only.
prerequisites: 3 clean laps at this track so you have a reference.

steps.text: Drive › Radio › Braking calls: Off. Drive 3 laps, braking where you normally do.
Set Braking calls: All.
Drive 3 to 5 laps. Brake where you normally would; notice whether "brake" lands as you reach your braking point.
Optional: set Focus and drive 2 more laps.

attestations.text: No call came after my braking point

items.prompt: Did the calls land at or just before your braking points?
items.radio_brief: Validation: braking calls. Three laps with braking calls off, then three with them on.

informs.status_md: Verified vs unverified › Live braking cues: not yet validated live

items.rule_text: Each call's key word is measured where the iPad started playing it; more than 5 m past its aim (the engine's own margin) is late. Your braking is read from the stored lap: the nearest onset within 100 m (heuristic) of the call's point, by distance, never by corner name. This passes with 8 calls measured (heuristic) over 3 braking zones (heuristic), none late, at most 10 % more than 0.6 s early (heuristic) and at most 20 % lost in delivery (heuristic). Two late calls, or more than 10 % of the calls measured, fail. If you brake 10 m or more later (heuristic) with calls on than with them off (8 points each), the result is left for you to check: calls must never delay braking. AI-field heads-ups are counted apart.
items.unavailable_reason: Voice is off on this Mac.

items.title: Assetto Corsa on the PS5: laps timed and coached
items.summary: Four or more laps of AC on the PS5 through Pitwall's own client: timed, stored and coached.
items.why: Pitwall's own AC client and service have not run against the console yet.
prerequisites: Setup › Connect › Assetto Corsa on, platform PS5, the console's address filled in.
AC (PS4 version) running on the PS5.

steps.text: Start a practice session, one car, one track.
Drive out and do at least 4 full laps without pitting.
Compare the lap times on Review › Sessions with the game's.
Optional, stopped in the pit lane: the input check.

attestations.text: Pitwall's lap times match the game's to the millisecond

items.prompt: Were your laps timed and coached correctly?
items.radio_brief: Validation: Assetto Corsa. Four full laps without pitting, then compare the lap times.

informs.status_md: Other games › Assetto Corsa › Unverified: own client and service
informs.capability_row: Assetto Corsa (original, PS4 version) · PS5 (backward compatibility)

items.rule_text: Over every live AC session in this run: the handshake answered, 50 packets a second or more (heuristic), nothing rejected, 3 timed laps (heuristic) of which 2 clean (heuristic), the track length taken from a full lap, 3 corners learned and a coaching point, plus your tick that the times match. Five minutes on a known line with no timed lap, or any rejected packet, fails. The input check records the raw steer at full lock and whether reverse was seen, for the maintainer.

items.title: Gran Turismo 7 on the PS5
items.summary: Four or more laps of GT7 on one circuit: timed, stored and coached.
items.why: GT7 has only been tested with generated data.
prerequisites: Setup › Connect › Gran Turismo 7 on with the PS5's address.

steps.text: Time Trial or a race on one circuit (not a replay).
Drive 4 or more laps.
Compare lap times with the game's.
Optional: the input check.

attestations.text: Pitwall's lap times match the game's to the millisecond

items.prompt: Were your laps timed and coached correctly?
items.radio_brief: Validation: Gran Turismo 7. Four laps on one circuit, then compare the lap times.
items.rule_text: Over every live GT7 session in this run (GT7 starts a new session on each retry or loading screen): the heartbeat sent without errors, packets from the console, the packet variant, 50 packets a second or more (heuristic), nothing rejected, 3 timed laps on one circuit (heuristic) of which 2 clean (heuristic) and a coaching point, plus your tick that the times match. Streaming from menus is shown as streaming, not driving. The game's best lap is compared with Pitwall's as a warning only.

items.title: Game choice and the wrong-game banner
items.summary: Choose one game, drive another: a banner must say so, and go when you choose that game.
items.why: The game choice and its banner are new and have not been tried on the rig.

steps.text: Setup › Game: choose F1 25 on PS5.
Start another enabled game (for example GT7) and drive out.
Check that a banner says the data is from another game.
Choose that game: the banner must go.

items.prompt: Did the banner come and go as described?
items.radio_brief: Validation: game choice. Drive another game than the one chosen, then choose it.

informs.status_md: Game selection (the game-selection lane's status entry)

items.rule_text: While this test is current Pitwall reads the chosen and the detected game every second. It passes when a mismatch came on and later went.
items.unavailable_reason: This Mac has no game choice yet.

items.title: Switching drivers mid-session
items.summary: Two drivers share one session: each driver's laps must end up under their own name.
items.why: Splitting a session on a driver switch is verified on generated data only.

steps.text: Driver A drives 2 timed laps.
Switch to driver B from the driver button on Drive (pit lane or on track).
Driver B drives 2 laps.
Switch back to A.

attestations.text: I switched from the new dashboard

items.prompt: Did each driver's laps end up under their own name?
items.radio_brief: Validation: driver switch. Two laps each, switching from the driver button on Drive.

informs.status_md: Dashboard v2 › driver switching from the new UI

items.rule_text: For each switch during this test Pitwall reads the sessions before and after it: laps after the switch must be stored under the new driver, and the previous driver's braking calls must not stay armed. It passes with one switch that has laps on both sides.
items.unavailable_reason: Add a second driver in Settings › Drivers first.

voice_commands.does: Starts a run with every available test that is not optional
Moves to the next test (the current one keeps its state)
Marks the current test as worked
Marks the current test as didn't work
Says the current test and what it asks
Finishes the run and saves the report
